name: CRITICAL WARNING: Full-Strength In-Flight Carbonated Sodas (Boyle's Law Colic Expansion)
whyItWorks: CLINICAL WARNING: According to Boyle's Law, when aircraft cabin altitude drops to equivalent 6,000–8,000 feet, free gas in the human intestinal tract naturally expands by 25% to 30%. Drinking full-strength carbonated sodas introduces immense volumes of dissolved CO2 that aggressively expand in the bowel, causing severe gas colic, excruciating distension, and trapped gas at strictures.
prepOrOrderInstructions: Never drink full-can carbonated sodas or sparkling seltzers on airplanes. Stick to still bottled water or diluted juices.
